issue_context.title: Capture reference to blazor components with nullability enabled always gives warning on net5.0 preview 7
issue_context.body: When project nullability is enabled there is no way to capture a reference to a blazor component without generating a compiler warning. ### Steps to reproduce * Create template project: `dotnet new blazorwasm` * Edit project file, add `enable` * Build -> observe there are some nullable warnings, ignore these they can all be fixed by updating the code * In `Index.razor` add the following: ``` @code { SurveyPrompt p; } ``` * In `Index.razor` update the component line to read: `` * Build the project again -> observe warning line #7 `CS8618: Non-nullable field 'p' is uninitialized'` * Change declaration to: `SurveyPrompt? p;` * Build again -> observe warning line #7`CS8600: Converting null literal or possible null value to non-nullable type` There seems to be no way to get rid of this warning. If it was somewhere in c# code one could have added a pragma around the specific line, but since the warning is in the razor part of the file it cannot be disabled for that specific line only
comments:
I had a quick look into this just to understand it, since it was surprising. Possibly the issue is here:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/40869f8969dbbf24b7668f0284c6abbf40ce093c/src/Components/Components/src/Rendering/RenderTreeBuilder.cs#L589

The callback is typed as `Action<object?>`, which means the following generated code:

```cs
        __builder.AddComponentReferenceCapture(3, (__value) =>
        {
#nullable restore
#line 7 "C:\Users\stevesa\Desktop\BlazorP8StandupDemo\ServerApp\Pages\Index.razor"
            myInstance = (ServerApp.Shared.SurveyPrompt)__value;

#line default
#line hidden
#nullable disable
        }
```

... produces a warning because `__value` is `object?` and we're casting to a non-nullable type.

I suspect it would be correct to change the callback type to `Action<object>` because we know the framework will only pass nonnull values to it.
That was my conclusion as well @SteveSandersonMS.

review_comments: Why not make it a nullable string (`string?`)?
In this particular case, Summary is always initialized, so this better reflects the nullability of the property.
@pranavkm If I do `var forecast = new WeatherForecast();`, it won't be initialized. Giving it a default value of `string.Empty` could be better IMO.
